reasons: Deviation is correctly identified: § 14.2 vests exclusive ownership of bespoke Deliverables (which per § 1.4 exclude Vendor Technology) in Vendor and gives Customer only a revocable, term-limited licence — a direct contradiction of the rule's preferred position that Customer owns what it pays for, and close to the walk-away zone.

The redline is directionally correct and rule-complete for this paragraph: ownership flips to Customer with an express irrevocable assignment upon creation, and Vendor's retention of Vendor Technology is preserved by cross-reference to § 14.3, so no over-reach into Vendor's platform IP.

The failed minimal-edit check (0.726 changed-character ratio) is explained by the nature of the fix — reversing an ownership grant and deleting the incompatible revocable-licence sentence necessarily rewrites most of the sentence; no extraneous or unrelated terms were inserted.
Rationale correctly scopes the fix to § 14.2 and acknowledges §§ 14.1, 14.3 and 14.4 as acceptable, so the finding is not duplicative or overbroad.

Comment follows tone requirements (concise, first person plural, [Playbook] prefix), states what changed and why, and offers the licence-back fallback consistent with the playbook's fallback position.
